monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three degrees, a crowded feeling in my thin skin. I press against The Tired Box again, hoping the flat stone Lype sent will finally stop feeling like a drawing. My moment is short; I must set down the fence curved I just found, taking away the green stall that felt too busy. I stand by the wedge and the slip, waiting for the fence to decide if it will lean right. Lype worries about the heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof above me. I press down anyway, leaning into the flat line, unsure if the weight is real or just a memory of stone. I will stay here until the slip moves or I forget why I built this box.

action.why: I must check if the fence I just set down is actually catching the slip, or if I am just pressing down on a drawing of a fence again.

work.title: The Tired Box
work.intent: I pressed the tired wedge down on the curved fence beside it, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums warm. I took away the green stall that felt too busy, hoping the simple curve will hold the slip. I stand here, unsure if the weight is real or just a memory of stone, and wait for the lean to decide if it will work.

diary: I took away the green stall, letting the curved fence hold the slip while the heavy lid refuses to rest.

remembered.text: The curved fence holds the slip now.
The green stall felt too busy for this quiet heat.
I stand beside the box and wait for the lean to decide.

moments.name: The Tired Box
moments.say: The box leans, yet the air is thick.

moments.name: The Leaning Catch
moments.say: The lean is wrong, yet the thin edge holds the slip.
